news.content: Start Sport Switzerland International Football People MyTech Lifestyle Start Sport Switzerland International Football People MyTech Lifestyle LifestyleWhat You Need to Know About Chikungunya Fever A Treacherous Tropical Virus First Cases in Switzerland—Here's What You Need to Know About Chikungunya Fever 02:02 Kampf gegen die Tigermücke: USA setzen auf Bakterien – die Schweiz auf sterile Mückenmännchen For the first time, four people in Switzerland have been infected with the chikungunya virus. The virus is transmitted by the tiger mosquito. How dangerous is the disease, what symptoms does it cause, and how can you protect yourself? Britta Gfeller 05.11.2026, 12:42•05.11.2026, 15:21 Here's what it's all about The chikungunya virus is transmitted by tiger mosquitoes. Local infections have been detected in Switzerland for the first time, but the risk of infection remains low. Typical symptoms of chikungunya include high fever, severe joint and muscle pain, and headaches. The disease is usually mild, but joint pain can last for months. The best ways to protect against chikungunya are mosquito repellent, long clothing, and mosquito nets. In Switzerland, a vaccine is also approved and recommended for travel to areas currently experiencing outbreaks. Summary created with In Ticino, there have been the first confirmed cases of people have been infected with the chikungunya virus within Switzerland. On Wednesday, Ticino health authorities confirmed four locally acquired infections in the Magadino Plain near Bellinzona. The infections are believed to have occurred at the end of summer. According to the Ticino University of Applied Sciences (SUPSI), the four affected individuals live on the same street. How is the virus transmitted? The virus is transmitted through mosquito bites, primarily those of the tiger mosquito. This species is native to the tropical and subtropical regions of South and Southeast Asia, but has also spread to many other regions of the world. It has been present in Switzerland since the early 2000s. The infections in Ticino are so-called “autochthonous cases,” as reported by the Corriere del Ticino reports, citing SUPSI. This means that a mosquito found in Ticino bit a person who had previously been infected in a high-risk area and had subsequently returned to Switzerland. The mosquito picked up the virus and transmitted it to other people through subsequent bites. The disease cannot be transmitted directly from person to person. What are the symptoms? According to the Federal Office of Public Health (FOPH), the disease usually develops seven to nine days after being bitten by an infected mosquito. Symptoms include high fever, severe joint and muscle pain, and headaches. Sometimes a rash also develops. How dangerous is the virus? According to the BAG, infection with the chikungunya virus is generally not dangerous. In rare cases, however, it can lead to prolonged fatigue and debilitating joint pain lasting weeks or months. In some cases, severe symptoms have been observed in newborns, older adults, and people with chronic illnesses. According to the Corriere del Ticino, the four people who contracted the virus in Switzerland are recovering well. Aside from persistent joint pain, they are doing fine. Symptoms include high fever, severe joint and muscle pain, and headaches. Sometimes a rash also develops. How dangerous is the virus? (File photo) Keystone At the moment, the risk to the public posed by the chikungunya virus is low, says Ticino’s cantonal medical officer Giorgio Merlani in an interview with the Keystone-SDA news agency. However, Switzerland will need to be prepared for the future. Keystone-SDA 07.11.2026, 09:01 Keystone-SDA: Giorgio Merlani, when did the four people affected by chikungunya fever test positive? Giorgio Merlani: “In mid-October, the chikungunya virus was detected in the blood of the patients. When the doctor encountered two other positive cases of the chikungunya virus in October, he recalled this case and tested that person as well.” Why is that? Do they all have the same doctor? Merlani: “Two of the four people who fell ill are related. The other two live nearby.” How are the four patients doing now? Did they have to be hospitalized? Merlani: “Fortunately, all four are doing quite well. They only had to go to the hospital for tests. Two of them mainly had the typical rash, while the other two mainly suffered from body aches.” Do you expect more locally transmitted cases to occur in the coming weeks? Merlani: “No, I don’t expect that to happen right now. But you should never say ‘never.’ There are only a few mosquitoes around at the moment. In addition, in collaboration with the University of Applied Sciences and Arts of Southern Switzerland (SUPSI), we’ve sprayed a substance in the residential area where those affected live that kills adult tiger mosquitoes. Furthermore, not a single tiger mosquito in Ticino has tested positive for the chikungunya virus so far.” Is it possible to kill the mosquitoes in question using a substance sprayed locally? Merlani: “Yes, that’s very effective, because a tiger mosquito flies a maximum of about 100 meters in its entire lifetime. Thanks to this measure and the onset of winter, the risk of contracting the chikungunya virus is low at the moment. But the outlook for the future is different. We need to be prepared. The four cases in Ticino are a wake-up call for Switzerland.” In your opinion, what measures will be necessary in the future? Merlani: “In addition to the usual, individual preventive measures against the proliferation of tiger mosquitoes, municipalities must also fulfill their responsibilities. In Ticino, some are already collaborating with SUPSI to release sterile male tiger mosquitoes. In addition, under SUPSI’s leadership, efforts are being made to control tiger mosquito larvae. Numerous egg-laying traps distributed throughout the canton also map the density, activity periods, and spread patterns of the mosquitoes. All of this has proven to be effective. However, caution is also advised for travelers arriving from areas with many cases of the chikungunya virus.” What should be done about this? Merlani: “If vacationers test positive for the chikungunya virus, they must cover themselves so that tiger mosquitoes cannot bite them. This is because the mosquitoes transmit the virus to other people after about a week.” Is Ticino once again a “gateway” for a new virus? Merlani: “Not necessarily; tiger mosquitoes are also present in German-speaking and French-speaking Switzerland. The four cases in Ticino represent a very limited outbreak. But the virus will return, and we will see larger outbreaks. It’s important that we’re prepared for this throughout Switzerland.” The Ticino health authorities, in collaboration with SUPSI and the Federal Office of Public Health (FOPH), have launched a surveillance program for the West Nile virus. The goal is to reduce the risk of new cases of West Nile virus; SUPSI’s Institute of Microbiology serves as the national center of expertise. Should the federal government take further action? Merlani: “The federal government should, if possible, support preventive measures against the tiger mosquito. Cases of dengue fever could also occur in the future. I would be more concerned about this disease than about chikungunya fever. analysis.brief_en: In Ticino, Switzerland, four individuals have tested positive for chikungunya fever, with two cases identified in October and one previously symptomatic in August. The cantonal medical officer, Giorgio Merlani, emphasizes the need for preventive measures against the Asian tiger mosquito, which also transmits dengue fever. All four patients are recovering well without hospitalization, and the current public risk is low due to winter conditions and local mosquito control efforts. However, Merlani warns that the virus may return with larger outbreaks in the future. The response includes spraying to eliminate adult mosquitoes, releasing sterile males, and monitoring larvae. A surveillance program for the West Nile virus is also underway. Merlani urges the federal government to support preventive actions and highlights the potential for dengue fever cases, which he considers more dangerous than chikungunya. The cases serve as a wake-up call for Switzerland to prepare for future outbreaks.

news.content_zh: 在瑞士提契诺州,四人 基孔肯雅热 检测呈阳性,其中 2 例于 10 月发现,1 例曾于 8 月出现症状。该州医疗官员乔治·梅拉尼(Giorgio Merlani)强调需要对亚洲虎蚊采取预防措施,这种蚊子也会传播登革热。所有四名患者均康复良好,无需住院,由于冬季条件和当地蚊虫控制工作,目前的公共风险较低。然而,梅拉尼警告说,该病毒将来可能会以更大的 暴发 卷土重来。应对措施包括喷洒药物消灭成年蚊子、释放不育雄性蚊子以及监测幼虫。针对西尼罗河病毒的 监测 计划也在进行中。梅拉尼敦促联邦政府支持预防行动,并强调登革热病例的可能性,他认为登革热比基孔肯雅热更危险。这些案件为瑞士敲响了警钟,为未来的 暴发 做好准备。

Follow us News Arena Network - Ranchi - UPDATED: July 13, 2026, 09:00 AM - 2 min read Every district has also been asked to prepare a detailed action plan and submit it to the state headquarters, with dengue and chikungunya control being treated as a priority. The Jharkhand government has stepped up its preparedness against dengue and chikungunya, directing all district administrations to remain on high alert as the monsoon season increases the risk of mosquito-borne diseases. The Department of Health, Medical Education and Family Welfare has issued a statewide advisory asking Deputy Commissioners to launch immediate preventive measures and intensify surveillance to curb the spread of infections. Additional Chief Secretary Ajay Kumar Singh has instructed district authorities to focus on vulnerable and waterlogged areas where mosquito breeding is more likely. He has asked officials to ensure that breeding sites are identified and eliminated on priority to prevent a rise in cases during the rainy season. The advisory notes that both dengue and chikungunya are viral illnesses transmitted through the bite of the female Aedes mosquito, which breeds in clean, stagnant water. Common breeding grounds include water stored in coolers, uncovered tanks, buckets, plastic containers, discarded bottles, old tyres and other items where rainwater accumulates. The department has stressed the need for regular cleaning of such locations and prompt removal of stagnant water. To strengthen the prevention drive, the Health Department has directed municipal corporations, municipal councils, district administrations, Multi-Purpose Workers (MPWs), Sahiyas and community volunteers to work in coordination to detect and destroy mosquito breeding sites. Every district has also been asked to prepare a detailed action plan and submit it to the state headquarters, with dengue and chikungunya control being treated as a priority. Door-to-door vector surveillance will form a major part of the campaign. Health workers will inspect residential areas to identify mosquito larvae and eliminate breeding sources. Districts have also been instructed to ensure the availability of essential surveillance equipment, including plastic dippers, pipettes and larva collection vials. The department has appealed to residents to play an active role in preventing the spread of the diseases by ensuring that water does not stagnate in or around their homes. People have been advised to clean coolers and water storage containers regularly, keep overhead tanks covered and seek medical attention at the nearest health facility if they develop fever, instead of resorting to self-medication. news.source_body_en: The Jharkhand government has issued a statewide advisory to address the heightened risk of dengue and chikungunya during the monsoon season. The advisory, published on November 9, 2026, emphasizes the need for immediate preventive measures and intensified surveillance to curb the spread of these mosquito-borne diseases. The Department of Health, Medical Education and Family Welfare directed Deputy Commissioners to focus on vulnerable and waterlogged areas where Aedes mosquitoes breed in stagnant water. Common breeding sites include coolers, uncovered tanks, buckets, and discarded bottles. The government has instructed municipal corporations, district administrations, and community volunteers to work together in detecting and destroying mosquito breeding sites. Health workers are tasked with inspecting residential areas for larvae and eliminating breeding sources. Districts have also been asked to ensure the availability of surveillance equipment such as plastic dippers and larva collection vials. Residents are urged to clean water storage containers, keep overhead tanks covered, and seek medical attention promptly if they develop fever symptoms. The advisory underscores the importance of public participation in preventing the spread of these diseases, especially during the rainy season when mosquito activity increases.
news.content_zh: 贾坎德邦政府发布了一项全州咨询,以应对季风季节登革热和基孔肯雅热的高风险。该通报于 2026 年 11 月 9 日发布,强调需要立即采取预防措施并加强 监测 以遏制这些蚊媒疾病的传播。卫生、医学教育和家庭福利部指示副专员重点关注伊蚊在死水中繁殖的脆弱和积水地区。常见的繁殖地点包括冷却器、未加盖的水箱、水桶和废弃的瓶子。政府已指示市政公司、地区管理机构和社区志愿者共同努力,发现并摧毁蚊子滋生地。卫生工作者的任务是检查居民区是否有幼虫并消除繁殖源。还要求各地区确保 监测 设备的可用性,例如塑料铲和幼虫收集瓶。敦促居民清洁储水容器,盖好头顶水箱,如果出现发烧症状,请立即就医。该建议强调了公众参与预防这些疾病传播的重要性,特别是在蚊子活动增加的雨季。

analysis.brief_en: Four local cases of chikungunya fever were confirmed in Ticino, Switzerland, according to an announcement by the Ticino Department of Health and Social Affairs on Wednesday, November 4, 2026. The chikungunya virus, transmitted by the tiger mosquito, has been locally spread for the first time in Switzerland. The affected individuals had not recently traveled to areas where the virus is circulating, and they showed a favorable clinical course, with persistent joint pain being the main symptom. The current public risk is considered very low, partly due to the small number of cases and the approaching end of the mosquito season. The Office of the Ticino Cantonal Medical Officer, along with SUPSI, municipal authorities, and federal agencies, has launched epidemiological investigations and mosquito control measures in the affected areas. This development marks the first local transmission of the chikungunya virus in Switzerland, highlighting the need for continued vigilance and preventive actions.

supplementary_news.content: Start Sport Switzerland International Football People MyTech Lifestyle Start Sport Switzerland International Football People MyTech Lifestyle Lifestyle"The chikungunya cases in Ticino are a wake-up call for Switzerland" Tiger mosquito "The chikungunya cases in Ticino are a wake-up call for Switzerland" The Ticino cantonal medical officer is calling for preventive measures against the Asian tiger mosquito, as this species also transmits dengue fever. (File photo) Keystone At the moment, the risk to the public posed by the chikungunya virus is low, says Ticino’s cantonal medical officer Giorgio Merlani in an interview with the Keystone-SDA news agency. However, Switzerland will need to be prepared for the future. Keystone-SDA 07.11.2026, 09:01 Keystone-SDA: Giorgio Merlani, when did the four people affected by chikungunya fever test positive? Giorgio Merlani: “In mid-October, the chikungunya virus was detected in the blood of the patients. One of the four people had already experienced symptoms consistent with the virus in August but did not get tested. When the doctor encountered two other positive cases of the chikungunya virus in October, he recalled this case and tested that person as well.” Why is that? Do they all have the same doctor? Merlani: “Two of the four people who fell ill are related. The other two live nearby.” How are the four patients doing now? Did they have to be hospitalized? Merlani: “Fortunately, all four are doing quite well. They only had to go to the hospital for tests. Two of them mainly had the typical rash, while the other two mainly suffered from body aches.” Do you expect more locally transmitted cases to occur in the coming weeks? Merlani: “No, I don’t expect that to happen right now. But you should never say ‘never.’ There are only a few mosquitoes around at the moment. In addition, in collaboration with the University of Applied Sciences and Arts of Southern Switzerland (SUPSI), we’ve sprayed a substance in the residential area where those affected live that kills adult tiger mosquitoes. Furthermore, not a single tiger mosquito in Ticino has tested positive for the chikungunya virus so far.” Is it possible to kill the mosquitoes in question using a substance sprayed locally? Merlani: “Yes, that’s very effective, because a tiger mosquito flies a maximum of about 100 meters in its entire lifetime. Thanks to this measure and the onset of winter, the risk of contracting the chikungunya virus is low at the moment. But the outlook for the future is different. We need to be prepared. The four cases in Ticino are a wake-up call for Switzerland.” In your opinion, what measures will be necessary in the future? Merlani: “In addition to the usual, individual preventive measures against the proliferation of tiger mosquitoes, municipalities must also fulfill their responsibilities. In Ticino, some are already collaborating with SUPSI to release sterile male tiger mosquitoes. In addition, under SUPSI’s leadership, efforts are being made to control tiger mosquito larvae. Numerous egg-laying traps distributed throughout the canton also map the density, activity periods, and spread patterns of the mosquitoes. All of this has proven to be effective. However, caution is also advised for travelers arriving from areas with many cases of the chikungunya virus.” What should be done about this? Merlani: “If vacationers test positive for the chikungunya virus, they must cover themselves so that tiger mosquitoes cannot bite them. This is because the mosquitoes transmit the virus to other people after about a week.” Is Ticino once again a “gateway” for a new virus? Merlani: “Not necessarily; tiger mosquitoes are also present in German-speaking and French-speaking Switzerland. The four cases in Ticino represent a very limited outbreak. But the virus will return, and we will see larger outbreaks. It’s important that we’re prepared for this throughout Switzerland.” The Ticino health authorities, in collaboration with SUPSI and the Federal Office of Public Health (FOPH), have launched a surveillance program for the West Nile virus. The goal is to reduce the risk of new cases of West Nile virus; SUPSI’s Institute of Microbiology serves as the national center of expertise. Should the federal government take further action? Merlani: “The federal government should, if possible, support preventive measures against the tiger mosquito. Cases of dengue fever could also occur in the future. I would be more concerned about this disease than about chikungunya fever. The first infection with dengue fever is usually mild, but a second infection can be quite dangerous.” Found an error?
